`python3 -m shop quote a:12.5:2` now prints `27.06`, and all 11 tests pass.

**Root cause:** `to_cents` in `shop/money.py:9` padded the fractional part on the left. `"12.5"` has fraction `"5"`, and `rjust(2, "0")` turned it into `"05"`, so the price became 1205 cents instead of 1250. The totals followed from that: 2 × 1205 = 2410, plus 199 tax, gives 2609, which prints as `26.09`. With the right price it is 2500 + 206 = 2706, which prints as `27.06`. The pricing and tax code was correct. Any one-decimal price was affected, so `0.5` also came out as 5 cents.

**Fix:** I changed `rjust` to `ljust`, so `"5"` becomes `"50"`. It is a one-line change.

**Tests:** I added `tests/test_money.py` with 5 tests, covering one-digit fractions, two-digit fractions, no fraction, too many decimals, and the exact CLI case from your report. The existing suite never touched `money.py`, which is why the bug got through. Two of the new tests fail on the original code and pass now. I checked that against a read-only export of `HEAD`, because my first attempt (`git stash push`) was blocked by a git guard that matched the word "push". Nothing was changed by that attempt.

**Not fixed:** `python3 -m shop` fails because there is no `shop/__main__.py`, so I used your fallback invocation. I haven't added one.

**Also noticed:** `to_cents` mishandles negative amounts. `"-12.50"` gives -1150 and `"-0.50"` gives +50, because the sign only applies to the whole part. Nothing in the repo passes negative prices today, so I left it alone.
